title: Donanemab-azbt injection
overview: Donanemab-azbt may cause a potentially serious reaction called amyloid related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), which most commonly includes temporary swelling in areas of the brain; small spots of bleeding on the surface of the brain and, infrequently, larger areas of bleeding in the brain may also occur. Swelling in areas of the brain usually does not cause symptoms and usually resolves over time. If you experience any of the following symptoms, tell your doctor immediately or get emergency medical treatment: headache, confusion, dizziness, vision changes, nausea, difficulty walking or loss of balance, or seizures.

sections.Before receiving donanemab-azbt,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to donanemab-azbt, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in donanemab-azbt injection. Ask your pharmacist or check the Medication Guide for a list of the ingredients.tell your doctor and pharmacist what prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breast-feeding. If you become pregnant while taking donanemab-azbt, call your doctor.
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: chills, redness of the skin, nausea, vomiting, difficulty breathing or shortness of breath, sweating, headache, chest pain, dizzinesshives, rash, itching, swelling of the lips, tongue, or throat, shortness of breath or difficulty breathingDonanemab-azbt may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
